test: per-shift player ratings: shift-TrueSkill team-agg (each shot = on-ice skater match, xGoal draw-band) + RAPM ridge team-agg (xGoal ~ sum on-ice off/def indicators, lambda 300, 3-season trail) + BLEND, over shipped model
note: ALL NULL n.s. (shift-TS +0.00001, RAPM -0.00000, blend +0.00001; TEST n=9218). corr(shiftTS,RAPM)=+0.12 (measure different things) but BOTH redundant with the xG team rating already in the model - player-level decomposition reconstructs the same team on-ice xG, noisier. DISPLAY also failed both ways: shift-TS deployment-confounded (top=defensive D Slavin/Lindell, classic plus-minus pathology - TrueSkill splits on-ice credit, can't isolate from linemates); RAPM baseline-absorbed (raw-xGoal response gives every O-player ~+0.012, ridge shrinks real diffs to noise -> flat, grinders on top). Pipeline (shifts 15.7M rows + 1.75M shots + on-ice reconstruction) built + reusable. NHL model stays 0.66418. Production player metric would need stint-based xG/60 RAPM (further build)

test: starting-goalie DELTA (tonight's starter GSAx/game vs the team's own recent-starter baseline EWMA) + absolute starter GSAx diff (control), over shipped model
note: BOTH NULL, well-powered (n=9780, cov 98%). Delta -0.00003 CI [-0.00036,+0.00030]; abs +0.00014 CI [-0.00039,+0.00067] both n.s. Properly scaled (std 0.164, 73% of games have meaningful delta, coef +0.197) so NOT a scaling artifact - a real null. WHY: goaltending is high-variance game-to-game (severe regression to mean); team xG rating already prices goalie context (xGA = suppression); NHL backups are still NHL goalies (small true-talent gap vs game noise); deployment (backups vs weak opps) partly cancels. SETTLES the 'live goalie is the #1 recoverable gap' hypothesis: it is NOT recoverable via GSAx ratings. Historical test uses actual starter ~= serve-time probable goalie, so the null generalizes to serving. Model stays 0.66418; gap-to-close is non-public info, not goalie identity
